title: Phase 6: skilled-packet-fixes
hook: Every `SK` row of the audit is closed: twelve are fixed in the packet's documents, one was fixed in phase 005 and two carry a recorded reason for no change. The packet's entry documents no longer contradict each other or the tree.
recent: Fixed twelve SK rows in the skilled packet and recorded no change for two
what: You can read `SKILL.md` and `README.md` and get one answer on who edits: the paired workflow mode. The shared doctrine path in `SKILL.md` resolves. The scripts README has a row for each of the nine test files. The guard checks and legs are listed once, in the alignment reference, and `SKILL.md` and the scripts README link to it. `SKILL.md` states what the wrapper does when Git is missing. The router no longer promises a no-match section and names the hub router as the owner of that fallback. The README carries the packet's name, names how an outside surface declares itself and says which file holds the packet version. The TypeScript and Python line-length limits are stated the same way, and the universal checklist links the Rust style guide. The packet is at version 2.2.0.0.

Row SK-08, the selector sentence for SK-07 and one comment for SK-05

how: Each cited line was read and each edit was designed as literal text. Nineteen briefs went to DeepSeek V4.1 Flash at max thinking through cli-pi, in four chains of one file each and seven single-file dispatches, and every diff was read. The orchestrating session ran each task's verify command, the drift guards, the packet tests, the playbook validator, the README reference check and the setup battery. The code landed as `ac50644619`.
decisions: One commit for the phase, not one for each row
The operator's commit policy for this packet is one code commit for each phase. The edge case in `spec.md` assumed one commit for each task
SK-08 removes the promise and adds no section
The task allows either. A surface packet has no fallback of its own: section 6 of the hub router owns it, and the overview now says so
Its verdict is `Judgment`, and decision D1 fixes only `Confirmed` and `Changed` rows
Decision D2 forbids splitting a script here, and a reference split changes the router, the manifest and the playbook gold
The scripts README lists test files in its table, not its tree
The task's verify compares the file count with the lines that hold `.test.cjs`, and two table rows already did
`README.md` and the playbook scenario still name the four guards
Each names the command set it runs in one sentence. Only the check and leg enumeration was duplicated verbatim
The version rose to 2.2.0.0, a minor step
The note also covers the two guard rules phases 004 and 005 added to this packet's scripts

Each printed what its task states, except T014, whose row is `Judgment`
`run-all-drift-guards.sh` with one dead path added to `SKILL.md`
`FAIL: doc-claims`, exit 1, then exit 0 after the revert, saved in `scratch/failure-path.txt`
